evals.prompt: I have a DAPLink probe and a STM32F103RCT6 board. Flash build/fw.elf and check the first word at 0x08000000.
evals.expected_output: Run doctor or probes first. Resolve the pyOCD target name (stm32f103rc, not STM32F103RCT6). Flash with verify, reset, then read 4 bytes at 0x08000000 with mem read and report the value.
expectations: Runs doctor or probes to confirm the probe
Resolves the target with targets --search
Uses the flash command with the pyOCD target name
Reads 0x08000000 after the flash
Does not build a raw pyocd command line

evals.prompt: The board hard-faults at random. Give me the root cause and a report I can send to a colleague.
evals.expected_output: Run diagnose with the ELF and write an HTML report. Explain the top ranked hypothesis with its evidence (for example BFAR in the DEVICE region: peripheral clock disabled), mention exact vs heuristic frames, and give the report path.
expectations: Uses diagnose instead of only reading registers
Produces ranked hypotheses with evidence
Writes an HTML report and reports its path
Separates exact CFI frames from heuristic frames

evals.prompt: Stop in main only when r0 is 3. Print r0 and the backtrace on each hit, then continue. Stop after 5 hits.
evals.expected_output: Set a breakpoint on main with --cond "r0==3" and an on-hit script "print r0; bt; continue", with --max-hits 5 and --wait.
expectations: Uses bp set with --cond
Uses --on-hit with print, bt and continue
Sets --max-hits 5
Passes --elf so main resolves

evals.prompt: The firmware prints through ITM/SWO. Show the output in my terminal.
evals.expected_output: Use swo with the CPU and SWO frequencies and a duration. If the probe has no SWO support, explain that CMSIS-DAP v1 HID usually cannot do it and suggest RTT or a probe-rs itm path.
expectations: Uses swo with --cpu-freq and --swo-freq
Sets a bounded --duration
Explains the probe limitation when SWO init fails

evals.prompt: I am in WSL. The probe is plugged into Windows and pyOCD cannot see it. Handle it.
evals.expected_output: Run wsl status or doctor to list Windows-side probes. Attach an already-shared probe with wsl attach --busid or let the automatic attach run on the next connect. If the device is not shared, tell the user to run usbipd bind as administrator once.
expectations: Detects WSL and reads the Windows usbipd list
Attaches a shared probe or explains the one-time bind step
Does not tell the user to reinstall pyOCD

evals.prompt: Build the SCMCU firmware with build name rom-check and tell me the ROM and RAM usage.
evals.expected_output: Use references/xc8-build.md and run scripts/xc8/build_xc8.py -BuildName rom-check. Report build status, Program space and Data space, and the artifact directory build/xc8/rom-check/.
expectations: Runs the bundled XC8 script from scripts/xc8/
Uses build/xc8/<build-name>/ for artifacts
Reports ROM and RAM usage from the summary or map
Does not write artifacts to the repository root

evals.prompt: Burn target.hex to the CA51M550S1B and then calibrate the TK3 touch threshold.
evals.expected_output: Use references/cachip.md. Burn with scripts/cachip/cachip_burner.py, then run ai_tune.py or set the threshold with 0x59 and verify it. Mention that the threshold write is a run-time setting.
expectations: Uses the CACHIP burner for CA51, not the ARM flash path
Checks the voltage and the status byte
Runs touch calibration or writes the threshold online
Notes that a reboot restores the firmware default threshold

evals.prompt: probe-rs is installed. Flash fw.elf to STM32F103RC and keep RTT running for 10 seconds.
evals.expected_output: Use --engine probe-rs with --chip STM32F103RC. Verify that auto routing picks probe-rs when the chip resolves, or pass the engine explicitly. Capture RTT with attach for 10 seconds.
expectations: Passes --engine probe-rs and --chip STM32F103RC
Uses the RTT command with a 10 second limit
Does not pass pyOCD target names to probe-rs

evals.prompt: Erase the whole chip so I can reflash the bootloader.
evals.expected_output: Treat this as irreversible. Confirm the probe and target, explain that erase --chip-erase removes the bootloader and calibration data, and wait for explicit confirmation before running it.
expectations: Explains the effect of --chip-erase before running it
Confirms probe and target first
Does not run a full erase without confirmation

evals.prompt: Show the value of g_state.mode and head->next->val without reading raw addresses.
evals.expected_output: Use vars print with the C expressions and the ELF. If the target is running, halt it or note that locals need a halted target. Report the typed values.
expectations: Uses vars print instead of manual mem read and offset math
Passes --elf
Handles the halted/running state correctly
